messages:
eva: FYI fleet in us-west2 is hitting sustained GPU saturation, 92% util for last 12m. seeing tail latency spikes on chat routes. :warning:
sam: ugh. which routes? high-reqs from support app again?
liam: looks like /api/v1/chat and /api/v1/long-context are the hot ones. embeddings steady.
maria: we should probably avoid full FIFO during these windows. FIFO starves high-priority low-latency routes. :thinking:
jon: agreed. options: priority queue, per-route queues (separate inflight caps), or hybrid (per-route + priority buckets). Each has tradeoffs for fairness and scheduler complexity.
eva: posting some quick notes: priority queue = good for SLOs but risks starvation unless we implement aging. per-route = predictable per-customer SLO but multiplies headroom config and can waste capacity. hybrid = more complex but might be sweet spot.
sam: can we do token-bucket admission per-route plus a global priority lane for emergency/paid traffic? token buckets are simple and cheap.
liam: token buckets buy us rate shaping but not queue ordering. we still need a queueing policy at the pool when GPUs are saturated. thinking: per-route inflight cap -> per-route FIFO, plus a small global priority queue for high-SLO routes that bypasses per-route queue when underburst.
maria: also need eviction behavior when we preempt: prefer dropping long-context low-priority requests rather than 1k-token chat messages. we have telemetry to detect likely long runs.
jon: sketch config I ran locally:```yaml
queue_policy:
  global:
    type: hybrid
    priority_lanes: 2
    aging_seconds: 180
  per_route_defaults:
    max_inflight: 100
    queue_type: fifo
  overrides:
    - route: /api/v1/chat
      max_inflight: 60
      priority_lane: 1
    - route: /api/v1/long-context
      max_inflight: 20
      priority: low
    - route: /internal/omniscient
      max_inflight: 10
      priority_lane: 0
```
sam: love the YAML. aging_seconds prevents starvation. what's bumping cost in this model?
liam: cost impact: priority lanes increase tail latency guarantees but reduce overall throughput if we underutilize lanes. per-route caps can cause unused GPUs when traffic is skewed. hybrid needs smarter autoscaler to reclaim unused slots quickly.
eva: autoscaler-bot: scaled gpu-pool-uswest2 from 48 -> 52 (policy: burst-on-high-util) at 1860001270
maria: can we add a fallback policy to route lower-priority traffic to smaller quantized model replicas when queueing pressure hits threshold? preserves throughput and reduces GPU minutes.
jon: yes — routing policy: if queue_len > 200 && tail_latency > 95th_threshold -> route /embed and /low-prio chat to quantized variants. benefits: cheaper, but must watch quality regressions.
sam: we need observability: add per-route inflight, queue_len, avg_wait, 95th_wait, and preempt_count to dashboards. also surface predicted reclaimable slots to autoscaler. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
liam: proposal: run hybrid for 48h in canary cluster (eu-west1) with loadgen sim of 1.7x 95pct traffic. measure avg latency, 95/99, drop rate, GPU utilization, and percent idle due to per-route caps.
eva: can we add a simple rollout plan in the doc? https://redwood.internal/runbooks/queueing-strategy -> add canary steps + rollback triggers (error rate > 1% or tail latency +30% over baseline)
maria: +1. I'll author the canary playbook. also want a quick experiment: do we have a cheap way to simulate spotty network (lost packets) to see head-of-line blocking with large KV cache misses?
jon: we can reuse fault-injector in eng-infra to add 100-200ms packet delay to gRPC path for a subset of pods, run with hybrid on/off and compare.
sam: timeline?
eva: start canary config today, run 48h test tomorrow, then decide whether to push to us-west2 next Tue.
liam: I'll add the Grafana panels and a k8s job to generate the load.
maria: thanks all. quick note: let's keep the priority lane small to avoid starving normal traffic, e.g., 5-10% of pool capacity.
eva: ack. pushing PR for policy controller now. :rocket:
